newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end mixed in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end mixed in thin trading.

text.p: Italian stocks closed mixed in thin trade on Monday with the all-share Mibtel index ending 0.07 percent up at 9,633, but off a day's high of 9,663, and with the Mib30 blue chip index down 0.03 percent at a day's low of 14,446 on late selling.
Traded volume was estimated at only around 350 billion lire.
Some dealers said market attention was focused on the passage of the Italian government's tough and controversial 1997 budget through the lower house of parliament.
Fiat group units Snia Bpd and Sorin Biomedica were both suspended limit up when they touched a 10 percent ceiling.
Sorin heads up the bio-engineering activities of chemical holding Snia Bpd. Traders said both stocks were recovering from sharp losses seen in recent weeks with some renewed talk of restructuring.
Fiat itself closed 1.41 percent off at 3,973 lire.

Television and advertising group Mediaset was up 1.99 percent at 7,270 lire but in thin business after news of the $20 billion merger between MCI of the U.S. and British Telecom, a partner in the Italo-British Albacom joint venture.
State-controlled energy giant ENI ended 0.41 percent down at 7,226 lire.

In firmer telecoms, mobile phone operator TIM closed 1.41 percent up at 3,172 lire against a high for the day of 3,215 lire after TIM CEO Vito Gamberale said 1996 results would be in line with the first half when TIM reported a 48 percent jump in profits. Telephone operator Telecom Italia closed 0.65 percent up at 3,414 and Stet telecoms holding up 0.84 percent at 5,303.

Banks and insurances were mixed, with Ambroveneto up 5.08 pct at 3,205 and Banca Commerciale Italiana down 0.23 pct at 2,607. Fiat group insurance company Toro gained 3.06 percent to 19,900 but Generali lost 0.56 percent to 29,107 lire.
